rationale: ROUND 2 of trail a44d9eb8 (round 1 = REVISE, gated by bug_historian). The change is now COMMITTED (80b9c6235) because HEAD was broken and this was the fix — see the last paragraph. Every round-1 objection is answered in code, not in argument; where a seat was right I say so and where a claim of mine did not hold I withdraw it. THE DEFECT, unchanged. RenderTemplateReportingMissing (component_library.go) executed a component template with text/template and, on ANY error, logged at Warn and silently fell back to a regex renderer written for HANDLEBARS syntax: it substituted {{.field}} values and left every {{if}}, {{range}} and {{end}} it could not execute in the output. Well-formed HTML, values resolved, control directives intact. Nothing downstream could tell a rendered page from an unrendered one; only validate_content noticed, refusing the whole page with up to 20 'blockers' that are a regex cap (FindAllString(html, 10)), not a measurement. [MEASURED 2026-08-19 20:45Z] 26 events, 7 domains, 25 work items, 08-11 15:39Z to 08-18 23:36Z, 24 parked at needs_human_review, accelerating. Every occurrence was an EXECUTE error — one content field of the wrong shape, never a broken template. WHAT CHANGED SINCE ROUND 1, objection by objection. (1) editquality + guardian, the three call sites the plan named and gave no edit: ALL THREE ARE NOW IMPLEMENTED — assemble_from_library.go fails the step, component_instance_conversion.go's GateConvertedTemplate propagates, and cmd/component-render-check routes BOTH a failed baseline and a failed per-field probe to its existing `unanalysed` bucket. That last one is the risk the seat and I both flagged and it is worth stating plainly: the audit's probe deliberately REMOVES a field and re-renders, so under the new seam that render can error, and an errored render returns "" whose shapeCounts are all zero — i.e. indistinguishable from 'this field is safely gated'. Left unhandled, the strictest possible seam would have quietly made the audit find FEWER defects. It is recorded per field in a bucket that already refuses --write-baseline and counts a component's baseline keys as uncovered rather than fixed. (2) bug_historian, GATING, the missingkey=zero absent-field sibling: SCOPED OUT AND REGISTERED AS A KNOWN-OPEN GAP, in the checker's own header, in the concept-register entry's landmine list, and in RFC_041 §5 — with the measurement the seat asked for rather than a reassurance. What covers the absent case today is missingRequiredLLMFields, and it runs at exactly TWO of the fifteen render call sites (v3_site_actions.go, the build path; rerender_page_sections_action.go, the rerender pre-check) and only for fields the schema marks BOTH source:"llm" AND required. Everywhere else, and for every optional field, an absent value still renders empty and silently. The seat is right that this platform's history makes missingkey=zero the wrong thing to call safe by default; the honest statement is that this change makes the MISTYPED shape loud and leaves the ABSENT shape exactly as it was. Extending the type checker to cover it was rejected for a reason the next paragraph makes concrete, not for convenience: absence is the presence gate's question at every declared type, and two gates answering it differently is how they drift. (3) bug_historian + guardian + render_guardian, 'reports complete but degraded' on the chrome store: NOW SURFACED THREE WAYS instead of a log line — the failing slot lands in the action result as chrome_render_failed (empty on every healthy run), a chrome_render_failed work item is filed at needs_human_review with NO handler and spec.still_serving so a reader can tell stale-but-serving from never-rendered, and the step FAILS OUTRIGHT when the site has nothing stored to serve. That last arm is a deliberate behaviour change for greenfield provisioning and is flagged as such in the register entry, exactly as the guardian seat asked. (4) bug_historian + render_guardian, the rerender carry with no consumer, and render_guardian's asymmetry point that a mistyped field breaking the render is the same class as a MISSING required field: ANSWERED BY USING THE SAME CHANNEL. A render failure now escalates the page to the writer through escalateRerenderToWriter — the same helper, the same needs_page item_key, the same content_data_backfill remedy that the missing-required-field pre-check in this very action already uses. Two differences, both deliberate and commented: it does not return early (the other sections re-rendered correctly and their bytes are worth saving), and a FAILED escalation does not fail the action (a record that gates the repair it describes is worse than a record that is missing — the same reasoning emitSectionDeadControlItem states for its own write). It is not new authority over content that works today: it fires only where a render ACTUALLY failed, a state that could not exist before this change because the fallback swallowed it. (5) reuse_agent, two objections, BOTH SUSTAINED AND ACTED ON. resolvedValueSatisfiesDeclaredType has been MOVED to datahelpers.DeclaredTypeSatisfied and is now the single leaf primitive for both declared-type questions on this estate — the resolver-fill one and the writer-output one — with its history carried over verbatim, because the seat was right that citing it as precedent while writing a parallel copy is the fork-path pattern. On the second: validateContentAgainstSchema is NOT prior art for a type checker despite its name — it tested required-field PRESENCE over a map[string]string in the legacy dialect, and missingRequiredLLMFields already superseded it; the deleted function's body is quoted in grounded_in so the seat can check rather than take my word. (6) prior_art_librarian, two claims, BOTH WITHDRAWN. 'A thirteenth seam nobody had named' is FALSE: the concept register already names RenderTemplateWithMap ('deliberately EXEMPT, named rather than silently skipped'), the bugs_open/238 lane enumerated it as one of eight unguarded call sites, and idea_uk_vm_site's own bug_historian seat FOUND it and routed it through the same <no value> detector. What is actually new is narrower and kept: its caller does html = contactInfoRe.ReplaceAllString(html, rendered), so an error DELETES the live contact block rather than mangling it — which revises 238's stated exemption reasoning, since 'its blast radius is a contact line' understates deleting the block — and its language DIVERGES from the component seam's (no FuncMap, no missingkey=zero, so {{safe}}/{{default}}/{{isset}} are PARSE errors there). And a second withdrawal this lane made against itself: the seam is currently UNREACHABLE. RenderTemplateWithMap <- rerenderInjectContactInfo <- rerenderSinglePage <- RerenderSitePagesAction, and RerenderSitePagesAction appears in NO entry of GlobalActionRegistry (320 handlers, checked 2026-08-19) — which is why the idea_uk lane measured the function as absent from the binary. It is a trap disarmed before the path is revived, not damage being stopped today. On the dead-URL precedent claim ('three seats independently demanded default-OFF'): CHECKED AGAINST THE CORPUS and it is TWO, not three — guardian and architecture objected to the unconditional record on council 98852baa; render_guardian's objection in that round was adjacent but different (that the rerender path records without refusing). The design is unchanged; the citation is corrected. (7) architecture, needs_rfc on the signature/contract change: RFC WRITTEN IN PARALLEL as that seat recommended, architecture_review/RFC_041_render_seam_error_contract.md, committed with the change. It states the old and new guarantee in one line each, records the four decisions so they are not re-litigated per call site, carries the prior-art corrections above, and ends with the question it exists to have decided — whether the one-line RenderTemplate wrapper should exist at all, which the 238 lane's round already called 'the RFC-shaped move, not a rider on a bug fix'. It also states what would have to be true for the change to have been wrong, as four re-runnable measurements with their falsifiers. (8) debug_historian, re-verify before merge rather than citing yesterday's numbers: RE-RUN. The census is 26/7/25 at 2026-08-19 20:45Z. The RFC_022 enumeration is 0 live consumers of refuse_mistyped_llm_fields AND 0 of refuse_dead_url_controls across 198 active non-snapshot agent_definitions, scanning default_config, task_workflow, orchestrator_workflow and orchestration_workflow. AND ONE NEW MEASUREMENT FOUND A DEFECT IN MY OWN CHECKER, which is the strongest thing this round has to report. Asking 'what population would the pre-render gate refuse today' returned 0 rows for top-level declared-array violations and 5 elements on ONE page for the nested case: fundamentallyai.com/production-backend-engineering, whose mechanism-flow section stores five steps[].branches as the EMPTY STRING. That page renders clean and has been deployed and serving since 08-15, because the template gates them ({{if $s.branches}} before the {{range}}). My first checker called that a violation — so an armed gate would have refused a rebuild of a healthy live page, and it is the only such row on the estate, so nothing but the census would have found it. Fixed by making the checker share ONE emptiness predicate with the presence gate: isEmptyContentValue moved to datahelpers.IsEmptyContentValue, so the two gates cannot disagree about the same field, which is the property my round-1 doc comment merely ASSERTED. WHY THIS IS ALREADY COMMITTED, stated because the gate should know. HEAD did not compile. ae7a8d739 (an unrelated section-editor claims-guard commit, 08:06Z) swept two lines of this work into HEAD as a same-file passenger, leaving section_editor_actions.go calling RenderTemplate with two returns while the seam still returned one; make build-* builds from committed HEAD, so every session's image build was broken. Verified in a clean git worktree, before and after. The commit carries Council-Submitted: a44d9eb8 (never Council-Reviewed on an unread verdict), and 098 credits it automatically if this round approves. A REVISE here is still worth having and will be acted on in a follow-up commit — the code is on the shared branch either way, which is this tree's normal condition and why review here is after the fact by design (owner ruling 2026-07-29 §2).

plan.summary: AS BUILT, commit 80b9c6235. The regex fallback is deleted and the component render seam returns an error, so a component render either EXECUTED or ERRORED and there is no third state; all fifteen call sites make an explicit failure decision in the diff. Returning "" was rejected as a second silent shape (assembleComponents would stitch a page with a section missing; GateConvertedTemplate would gate an empty render) — the compile break is the feature. datahelpers.ContentTypeViolations supplies the named diagnosis (indexed paths, recursion into `items` because the live case is nested), unconditionally as an ENRICHER on a render that has already failed and as an opt-in PRE-render refusal keyed refuse_mistyped_llm_fields with the unsafe default OFF. Two primitives were MOVED rather than duplicated (DeclaredTypeSatisfied, IsEmptyContentValue) so the type gate and the presence gate share one definition of 'wrong type' and one of 'empty'. Registered in the same commit: concept-register STY-057 with its index row, and RFC_041. Tests: the seam regression set (A/B pair, tool-page brace positive control that MUST pass, parse-error case, retired-dialect hard-fail, the contact-info language divergence, the conversion gate) plus nine checker units including the live empty-string row; mutation-proved by re-adding a one-line fallback, which fails 5 of them — and honestly, the conversion-gate test still passes under that mutation because it has a guard in series, which is recorded rather than glossed. Not in this change and stated as such: coercion/bounded repair (the writer half owns it — repairing at render time would permanently silence the only measure of the writer's violation rate), the absent-field sibling, and any output brace-scan (the design fires on a template engine error, never on the presence of braces, which is how the owner's tool-page ruling is satisfied by construction rather than by heuristic).

edits.symbol: RenderTemplateReportingMissing / RenderTemplate / RenderHeader / RenderFooter / RenderHead / Inject*
edits.rationale: The seam. On executeGoTemplate error, return the wrapped error at Error level instead of the regex fallback — the wrapped error already carries the template line, the field and the offending value. The three chrome renderers propagate into a ladder that ALREADY handled an error (InjectHeader/InjectFooter/InjectHead each answered err != nil with RenderFallbackX before this change), so chrome needed error PLUMBING, not new mechanism.
edits.sketch: Signatures now (string, []string, []string, error) and (string, error). The fallback block — contextToMap + renderEachBlocks + renderIfBlocks + renderGoStyleSubstitutions + renderHandlebarsSubstitutions + the {{nav_items_html}}/{{quick_links_html}} ReplaceAlls — is DELETED, and a tombstone comment stands where it was so the retired dialect is not re-authored. Also deleted, each verified caller-less: RenderTemplateWithValidation (dead), validateContentAgainstSchema, applyBidirectionalAliases. buildNavItemsHTML STAYS (render_site_components + the fallback chrome renderers use it). An EMPTY template still returns ("", nil): 'executed and produced nothing' is a different fact from 'could not execute', and rerender_page_sections carries a section on the first while failing on the second. contextToMap's death also removes bugs_open/203's last two fabricate-a-URL members (primary_cta_url -> /contact.html, secondary_cta_url -> /about.html). Inject* error branches now label the fallback — `<!-- HEADER SOURCE: fallback (render error) -->` — so provenance is greppable; the strip regex `<!--\s*HEADER\s+SOURCE:[^>]*-->` still matches it. InjectHead deliberately has no marker (the head is stripped and rebuilt by tag, so a comment before <head> would sit outside the element) and says so.

edits.rationale: The build path, where 25 of the 26 recorded events flow. Fails the step in the same shape as the missingRequiredLLMFields refusal twenty lines above and the dead-URL refusal just below, so the parked work item carries the CAUSE rather than 20 capped symptoms. Also the one site where the opt-in PRE-render refusal runs.
edits.sketch: On renderErr: ContentTypeViolations as an unconditional ENRICHER (it fires only because the render already failed, so it can refuse nothing that works), logged and appended to the returned error. Separately, inside the existing `if len(comp.InputSchema) > 0` block and immediately after the presence gate, the opt-in refusal gated on refuseMistypedLLMFields(config) (mistyped_llm_fields_gate.go, read exactly as shouldRefuseDeadURLControls reads its key, fail-OPEN on a non-bool). Spec: refuse_mistyped_llm_fields added to ConfigKeys — and refuse_dead_url_controls DECLARED at the same time, because this action has read it since bugs_open/238 shipped but through a helper rather than a literal config["..."], so the 2026-08-18 grep census could not see it. ⚠ CORRECTED from my round-1 comment, which claimed that blindness cost the RFC_022 budget: it does not. cmd/config-key-audit/optionalbudget.go:14-21 counts spec.Optional only and skips ConfigKeys on purpose ('settings rather than input references'), so neither flag moves the budget; what the declaration buys is the unknown-config-key report and this list's honesty.

edits.rationale: The repair vehicle. Carries the stored HTML on a render error through this path's OWN existing machinery (carryStoredSection, four sibling carry branches), and then escalates the page to the writer through the SAME helper the missing-required-field pre-check uses — which is render_guardian's asymmetry objection answered by reusing the existing route rather than inventing a second one.
edits.sketch: On renderErr: log Error with the type diagnosis, append the slot to resolution.RenderFailedSlots, carryStoredSection, carried++, continue. Surfaced as out["carried_render_failed"] beside carried_not_ready/carried_empty_template and named in describe(). After the loop, if RenderFailedSlots is non-empty: escalateRerenderToWriter(..., "a section's template could not execute against its stored content (bugs_open/260)") and out["escalation"]/out["escalated"]. The helper gained a `cause` argument for the human summary only — the spec's machine reason stays content_data_backfill and the item_key stays needs_page:<page> for BOTH callers, because the remedy is the same and the two causes should co-dedup on one page. NON-FATAL by design and commented as such: fatal() keeps its current membership, because a re-render that refuses on the state it was dispatched to fix deadlocks its own remedy. NO opt-in pre-render refusal on this path, deliberately and against my own round-1 plan: the checker keys on the schema rather than the template, so arming one here would carry a page that renders perfectly well — on the repair vehicle that is a regression, not a guard.

edits.rationale: The chrome STORE path has no gate downstream — whatever it stores is what the site serves. On a render error it does NOT store, so the existing row keeps serving, which is strictly better than replacing working chrome with chrome carrying unexecuted directives. Round 1's version reported that only in a log line inside a step that still returned success, which is the bugs_closed/028 / bugs_closed/040 shape three seats named; it is now surfaced in the result, filed as a work item, and escalated in the one case where nothing is serving.
edits.sketch: Signature gains a fourth return (renderErr error), non-nil for a render execution failure only; every other failure keeps its existing report-and-continue behaviour because every other failure leaves the stored bytes serving. The function files emitChromeRenderFailedItem (sibling of emitChromeDeadControlItem: shared insertWorkItem so it inherits the idx_swi_dedup-matched ON CONFLICT and the two-strike label; needs_human_review, NO handler; item_key chrome_render_failed:<site>:<slot>, carrying site+slot and NOT the component id so a repoint does not mint a second item for one defect; spec.still_serving so a reader can tell stale-but-serving from never-rendered) and returns the error. The caller collects slot -> error into the action result's chrome_render_failed map, and calls chromeSlotHasStoredHTML (new, one question, build_status deliberately NOT in the predicate — stale-but-serving bytes are still a fallback; a query error answers false, the conservative side) to decide escalation: any slot with nothing serving fails the step, naming every affected slot rather than the first. Note the pre-existing `if renderedHTML == ""` guard could never have caught this — the deleted fallback returned MANGLED html, never empty.

edits.rationale: The two UNGATED live-page routes, and the correction that matters most to the bug file: 'the gate is why there is no live damage' is true of the page-BUILD path only. updatePageComponentAfterEdit writes rendered_html straight to an already-live page with no validate_content between, and the `if rendered == ""` guard at both sites provably cannot fire for this defect. Returning the error refuses the edit and leaves the live row untouched.
edits.sketch: rendered, err := RenderTemplate(...); if err != nil { return sectionEditOutcome{}, fmt.Errorf("template rendering failed, live section left unchanged: %w", err) }; the empty-output guard is KEPT because an empty template is a different case. Same shape at applyComponentSwap with its 'after swap' wording. Exercised path, not theoretical: 271 content_rewrite/content_edit items, 117 complete, since 2026-04-08.

edits.sketch: assemble_from_library.go:297 — FAIL the step: no writer data is in scope on this path (the library supplies both template and data), so an execute error means a corrupt template, and a page assembled with a section silently missing is the bugs_open/018 class. component_instance_conversion.go:271 (GateConvertedTemplate) — PROPAGATE, so the RFC_034 acceptance gate can no longer green-light a template the real renderer cannot execute; a test also pins that a template whose {{range}} has no data must still PASS the gate, or it would refuse every data-less template. cmd/component-render-check/rendercheck.go:653,680 — a failed BASELINE render routes the component to the existing `unanalysed` bucket (which already refuses --write-baseline and counts that component's baseline keys as uncovered rather than fixed) and decrements `checked`; a failed PER-FIELD PROBE is recorded per field in the same bucket, never counted as a clean probe, because the probe deliberately removes a field and an errored render returns "" whose shapeCounts are all zero — the detector-blinding class this whole change exists to remove.

Its caller ReplaceAllStrings the LIVE contact-info block with the render result, so an error used to DELETE the block — worse than mangling it, and it leaves nothing for any detector to find. Returning the input HTML unchanged is the only behaviour that cannot make the page worse. PRIOR ART, corrected from round 1: this seam was already named by the concept register, by bugs_open/238's council round (which deliberately EXEMPTED it) and by the idea_uk_vm_site lane; what is new is the deletion behaviour and the language divergence.
edits.sketch: RenderTemplateWithMap returns (string, error) — parse and execute errors return ("", err) at Error instead of ("", nil) at Warn. Caller: on error, log Error and `return html` unchanged. The legacy head render at :532 sets headTemplate = "" on error and falls into the else-branch that already builds a complete fallback head. A comment at the seam records that the chain ends at RerenderSitePagesAction, which is in NO entry of GlobalActionRegistry (320 handlers, checked 2026-08-19) — so this is a trap disarmed before the path is revived, not damage stopped today, and anyone reviving it inherits both the deletion behaviour and the FuncMap divergence. A test pins the divergence: {{safe .x}} must FAIL here and PASS on the component seam, and it fails loudly if the two languages ever converge.

edits.rationale: The named diagnosis, pure so it is testable against live row bytes with no DB and no render. Recursion into `items` is mandatory rather than a refinement: the live case is NESTED (steps[2].branches), so a top-level-only check reports nothing for the very instance that motivated the change. This file is also where the reuse_agent seat's objection lands: it now OWNS both shared primitives instead of copying either.
edits.sketch: TypeViolation{Path, Declared, Actual} with indexed paths ('steps[2].branches: declared array (items: object), got string'). Rules: only source:"llm" fields (resolver fills have their own guard); declared array/list only ('list' is real, 5 live fields); BOTH live `items` dialects understood (JSON-Schema-ish with `properties`, 2 components incl. the motivating one; example-value maps, 12 components); elements of an items:object array must be maps, recursing for nested declared arrays; unknown/undeclared types skipped, never guessed; a declared SCALAR holding a map is NOT reported (text/template renders that without erroring, and this file explains render failures rather than grading content). MOVED IN: DeclaredTypeSatisfied (was actions.resolvedValueSatisfiesDeclaredType — history carried over verbatim, and the chrome path now calls the shared one) and IsEmptyContentValue (was actions.isEmptyContentValue, which is now a one-line alias) — the second is what stops the gate refusing a healthy live page, and its header records the fundamentallyai.com row that proves it. Tests: 9 units incl. the nested path, the A/B control, the live empty-string and whitespace cases, the example-value dialect, `list`, and five conservative-skip cases.

plan.risks: 1) THE ABSENT-FIELD SIBLING IS OPEN AND NAMED, not fixed: missingkey=zero still renders an absent field as empty and silently, and the presence gate covers 2 of 15 call sites and only required llm fields. Registered as a landmine in STY-057 and as a question in RFC_041 §5. 2) THE TYPE GATE IS SILENT FOR 75 OF 253 ACTIVE COMPONENTS (no schema at all) and 3 of the 110 exposed ones; the seam's error, not the gate, is the complete detector, and a green gate must never be reported as fleet coverage. 3) GREENFIELD CHROME BEHAVIOUR CHANGES: a first build whose chrome template cannot execute now FAILS instead of shipping the mangled render and reporting success. Deliberate, flagged to site provisioning, and the loanzy_uk_example_site lane is running a clean greenfield build after the roll and will report either way. 4) The rerender carry is non-fatal, so a page whose sections all fail re-saves its stored HTML and reports success with carried_render_failed — now mitigated by the writer escalation, but the page's own step still succeeds by design. 5) A dead-code path is being fixed defensively (the contact-info seam); if it stays unregistered, that edit never executes. Stated rather than presented as a save. 6) Two same-file passengers I could not exclude and named in the commit message: another lane's 26-line aliasing comment in rerender_page_sections_action.go, and the 000_concept_index.md rows. A pathspec commit cannot leave a same-file edit behind — and this morning that trap fired in BOTH directions on this very work (ae7a8d739 took two of my lines; my own commit then took another lane's uncommitted call site, briefly breaking HEAD a second way until I committed its definition as a declared sweep, a0bb2d867). 7) The arming migration must not be applied until an image carrying this commit has rolled; it is named _HOLD for that reason and the register entry says so. 8) go build ./... is clean and the actions + datahelpers packages pass; one UNRELATED pre-existing flake in v3_site_reconcile_identity_test.go fails on a different reconcile test each run in the shared working tree and passes 3/3 at clean HEAD in a worktree — it is another lane's uncommitted test edit, verified, and left as found.
